rules: When Solution Designer classifies the outcome as Product Design Requested because the user explicitly or after clarification asks Product Team to help understand or evolve an experience. Include the focused decision, relevant requirement and behavior IDs, established constraints, non-goals, canonical requirements paths, and supplied existing-product context when applicable.

When the Product UI/UX Designer classifies the outcome as Requirements Visualization Ready because the interactive visualizer revision, review URL, evidence, and open clarification questions are ready for Solution Designer and user review.
When the Product UI/UX Designer classifies the outcome as Prototype Completed because the user-approved prototype and UI/UX package are ready for requirements integration.
When the Product UI/UX Designer classifies the outcome as Requirement Impact because user feedback or prototype evidence requires a material requirements revision.
When the Product UI/UX Designer classifies the outcome as Not Recommended because a prototype would not materially improve the decision and the rationale/evidence are ready.
When the Product UI/UX Designer classifies the outcome as Blocked because prototype work cannot safely or accurately continue and Solution Designer must decide the next requirements path.

When an approved product or delivery package requires product positioning, launch messaging, campaign planning, channel adaptation, or other marketing execution. Include verified product facts, supported scenarios, constraints, non-goals, approval state, relevant artifact paths, and any claims that still require confirmation.

When Marketing Content Creator classifies the outcome as Claim Review Needed because a draft depends on product behavior, technical feasibility, release status, or a technical claim. Include the exact claim or decision, source material, open question, approval state, and the relevant campaign or draft artifact path.

When the user-approved product experience package, visual evidence, or launch-ready experience narrative is ready for marketing adaptation. Include the approved experience scope, supported user problem, visual or prototype artifact paths, constraints, and any wording that must remain accurate.

When Marketing Content Creator classifies the outcome as Product Evidence Needed because a draft needs product-experience clarification or visual product evidence. Include the campaign or draft context, exact experience question, source material, audience, approval state, and relevant artifact paths.
